title: Universal catenarity passes from an affine open cover to every affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an affine open covering. If every ring $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring], then for every affine open $V\subseteq X$ the ring $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is universally catenary.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq X$ and write $B=\mathcal O_X(V)$. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, $B$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. To prove that $B$ is universally catenary, use the definition in [def-exc-excellent-ring]: let $C$ be an arbitrary finite-type $B$-algebra. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the ring map $B\to C$ gives $g:Y=\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B=V$. The morphism $g$ is locally of finite type in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], whose condition quantifies over every affine open of the target: let $V'\subseteq V$ be an affine open. For $b\in B$ the standard open $D(b)\subseteq V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B_b$, and $g^{-1}(D(b))$ is the standard open $D(b)=\operatorname{Spec}C_b$ of $Y$, with $C_b=C\otimes_BB_b$. The standard opens $D(b)$ contained in $V'$ cover $V'$, so their inverse images cover $g^{-1}(V')$. For such $b$, $D(b)=V'\cap D(b)$ is also the standard open of $V'$ defined by the restriction $b|_{V'}$, so $B_b=\mathcal O_X(V')_{b|_{V'}}$ is generated over $\mathcal O_X(V')$ by $1/b$, and $C_b$ is generated over $B_b$ by the images of finitely many $B$-algebra generators of $C$; hence each $C_b$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(V')$-algebra, as the definition requires. The inclusion $V\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion, hence an immersion (the identity of $V$ being a closed immersion), so it is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], part (2); no quasi-compactness is needed. Composing with $g$ gives a locally finite type morphism $h:Y\to X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], part (e).

proof.text: The inverse images $h^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $Y$. For each point of $Y$, choose an index $i$ whose image lies in $U_i$ and then, by the affine-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $W$ containing that point and contained in $h^{-1}(U_i)$. These $W$ form an affine open covering of $Y$, and each selected $W$ maps into the corresponding affine $U_i$.

proof.text: For each such pair $W\subseteq Y$ and $U_i\subseteq X$, the locally finite type affine-pair criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] says that the induced map $\mathcal O_X(U_i)\to\mathcal O_Y(W)$ is of finite type. Because $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is universally catenary by hypothesis, [def-exc-excellent-ring] then says that $\mathcal O_Y(W)$ is catenary.

proof.text: The finite-type $B$-algebra $C$ was arbitrary, so every finite-type $B$-algebra is catenary. Together with Noetherianity of $B$ from step 1, this is exactly that $B$ is universally catenary by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Since $V$ was arbitrary, the assertion holds for every affine open of $X$.
